# package dpt

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-knx/dpt"
```

Package dpt encodes and decodes KNX datapoint types (DPT): the standardised representations of application values in group telegrams.

A datapoint type is identified by a main number (the format: 9 is the 2-octet float) and a subtype (the application semantics: 9.001 is a temperature in °C, 9.004 an illuminance in lux). [Lookup](#func-lookup) returns the [Type](#type-type) of an identifier from the registry; a Type encodes values to the octets of an A\_GroupValue\_Write or \_Response ([Type.Encode](#func-type-encode)), decodes them ([Type.Decode](#func-type-decode)), checks ranges, and formats and parses values as text with their unit.

Decoded values have these Go types, by [Kind](#type-kind):

	KindBool      bool                 DPT 1
	KindControl   Control              DPT 2
	KindStep      Step                 DPT 3
	KindChar      string (one rune)    DPT 4
	KindUnsigned  uint64               DPT 5 (unscaled), 7, 12
	KindSigned    int64                DPT 6, 8, 13, 29
	KindFloat     float64              DPT 9, 14, scaled 5/7/8/13 subtypes
	KindTime      TimeOfDay            DPT 10
	KindDate      Date                 DPT 11
	KindString    string               DPT 16, 234
	KindScene     uint8                DPT 17
	KindSceneControl SceneControl      DPT 18
	KindDateTime  DateTime             DPT 19
	KindEnum      Enum                 DPT 20
	KindBits      uint64 (bit set)     DPT 21, 22, 26
	KindRGB       RGB                  DPT 232
	KindRGBW      RGBW                 DPT 251
	KindXYY       XYY                  DPT 242
	KindAccess    AccessData           DPT 15
	KindOnOffInfo OnOffInfo            DPT 27
	KindVersion   Version              DPT 217
	KindSetpoints RoomSetpoints        DPT 222, 275

Encode accepts these types and, where unambiguous, convertible ones (any Go integer or float for a number, a name for an enumeration).

Decode accepts every value the format can carry; Encode also enforces the range of the subtype (9.001 decodes -300 °C, but refuses to encode it). Dates are checked field by field, not against the calendar.

Only subtypes whose semantics are published (KNX Standard volume 3/7/2, Datapoint Types) are registered; an unknown subtype of a known main type can still be used through [Lookup](#func-lookup) of the main type ("9"), which has the format of the family and no application semantics.

## Constants

```go
const Float16Max = 670433.28
```

Float16Max is the largest DPT 9 value that can be encoded: mantissa 2046, exponent 15 (0x7FFF, mantissa 2047, means "invalid data").

```go
const Float16Min = -671088.64
```

Float16Min is the smallest DPT 9 value: mantissa -2048, exponent 15.

## Variables

```go
var ErrFloat16Invalid = errValue("0x7FFF: invalid data")
```

ErrFloat16Invalid is the error of decoding 0x7FFF, the DPT 9 "invalid data" value.

## Functions

### func DecodeFloat16

```go
func DecodeFloat16(raw uint16) (float64, error)
```

DecodeFloat16 decodes the KNX 2-octet float format.

### func EncodeFloat16

```go
func EncodeFloat16(f float64) (uint16, error)
```

EncodeFloat16 encodes f in the KNX 2-octet float format: 0.01·M·2^E with a 12-bit two's complement mantissa M and a 4-bit exponent E, choosing the smallest exponent that fits, mantissa rounded to nearest (half away from zero).

## Types

### type AccessData

```go
type AccessData struct {
	// Code is the identification number 0..999999.
	Code uint32
	// Error is E: the detection failed.
	Error bool
	// Permission is P: access is granted.
	Permission bool
	// RightToLeft is D, the reading direction of the code: clear left to
	// right, set right to left.
	RightToLeft bool
	// Encrypted is C: the code is encrypted.
	Encrypted bool
	// Index is 0..15.
	Index uint8
}
```

AccessData is a DPT 15.000 value: an access identification code of six decimal digits (sent as BCD, most significant digit first) with its detection flags and an index.

#### func (AccessData) String

```go
func (a AccessData) String() string
```

String returns "012345 index=3", followed by the names of the set flags (error, permission, right-to-left, encrypted).

### type DateTime

```go
type DateTime struct {
	Year                 int // 1900..2155
	Month, Day           uint8
	Weekday              uint8 // 0 any day, 1 Monday .. 7 Sunday
	Hour, Minute, Second uint8 // Hour 24 only as 24:00:00

	Fault        bool // F
	WorkingDay   bool // WD
	NoWorkingDay bool // NWD: WD is not valid
	NoYear       bool // NY
	NoDate       bool // ND: month and day of month not valid
	NoWeekday    bool // NDoW
	NoTime       bool // NT
	SummerTime   bool // SUTI
	// ExternalSync is CLQ: the clock is synchronised to an external
	// source.
	ExternalSync bool
	// ReliableSource is SRC: the synchronisation source is reliable.
	ReliableSource bool
}
```

DateTime is a DPT 19 value with its quality flags.

#### func (DateTime) String

```go
func (d DateTime) String() string
```

String returns "2026-10-29 12:30:05".

### type ID

```go
type ID struct {
	Main uint16
	Sub  uint16
}
```

ID identifies a datapoint type: main number and subtype.

#### func ParseID

```go
func ParseID(s string) (id ID, hasSub bool, err error)
```

ParseID parses "9.001", "9.1", "DPT9.001", "DPT-9-1", "DPST-9-1" (the ETS notation) or a main number alone ("9", "DPT-9", main type with subtype 0 and HasSub false).

#### func (ID) String

```go
func (id ID) String() string
```

String returns "main.sub" with the subtype written with at least three digits ("9.001", "12.1200"); a subtype of 0 on a main type that has no subtype 0 is still written ("9.000").

### type Step

```go
type Step struct {
	// Increase is the direction bit: increase (3.007) or down (3.008).
	Increase bool
	StepCode uint8
}
```

Step is a DPT 3 value (dimming, blinds): a direction and a step code. StepCode 0 means break (stop); 1..7 divide the range into 2^(StepCode-1) intervals.

### type Type

```go
type Type struct {
	ID ID
	// Name is the KNX name, such as "DPT_Value_Temp".
	Name string
	// Description is a short human-readable description.
	Description string
	// Unit is the unit symbol of numeric types ("°C"), empty if none.
	Unit string
	// Bits is the size of the encoded value in bits (1, 2, 4, 8, 16...).
	Bits int
	Kind Kind
	// Min and Max bound numeric values when HasRange is set.
	Min, Max float64
	HasRange bool
	// Labels are the names of the two values of a DPT 1 subtype (false,
	// true), or of the enumeration values of a DPT 20 subtype.
	Labels []string
	// Enum maps the values of an enumeration to their names.
	Enum map[uint8]string

}
```

Type is a datapoint type of the registry.

#### func Lookup

```go

```

Lookup returns the type of an identifier: "9.001" a registered subtype, "9" the main type. An unregistered subtype of a known main type is not found; use the main type for its format.

Mains returns the main types, ordered by number.

#### func (Type) Decode

```go
func (t *Type) Decode(data []byte) (any, error)
```

Decode decodes the octets of a value. For small types data is the one octet of the APCI's low 6 bits; for the others it must have exactly [Type.Size](#func-type-size) octets.

#### func (Type) Encode

```go
func (t *Type) Encode(v any) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode returns the octets of v. For small types it returns one octet holding the value in its low bits.

#### func (Type) Format

```go
func (t *Type) Format(v any) string
```

Format returns v as text with its unit, as the CLI prints it: "21.5 °C", "on", "12:30:00".

#### func (Type) Parse

```go
func (t *Type) Parse(s string) (any, error)
```

Parse parses a value from text (the inverse of Format without the unit; a trailing unit is accepted): "21.5", "on", "true", "12:30:00", "2026-10-29", "#FF8000".

#### func (Type) Size

```go
func (t *Type) Size() int
```

Size returns the encoded length in octets (1 for small types).

#### func (Type) Small

```go
func (t *Type) Small() bool
```

Small reports whether values are sent in the 6 bits of the APCI octet (types of at most 6 bits).

#### func (Type) String

```go
func (t *Type) String() string
```

String returns "9.001 DPT\_Value\_Temp".
